Technical article · HTML series

HTML Integration with Other Technologies

How HTML works with the tools that surround it: CSS frameworks (Bootstrap, Tailwind CSS, Foundation), JavaScript frameworks (React, Angular, Vue), server-side template engines (Thymeleaf, Jinja2, EJS, Handlebars), server-side rendering and hydration, REST and GraphQL APIs, and browser testing tools (Selenium, Playwright, Cypress). Every library demo on this page runs on the real library, bundled into the file so it works offline.

Updated 15 November 2026121 references (Vancouver style)Includes exercises, trivia, a template lab, a rendering simulator, an API explorer, a test runner and a playground

The first article in this series showed that a browser only ever receives HTML, CSS and JavaScript, and the article on HTML APIs showed how scripts reach into the parsed document through the DOM. Very little production HTML is written by hand, though. It is produced by a template engine on a server, by a component framework in the browser, or by both, and it is styled by a CSS framework, fed by an API and checked by an automated browser. The HTML Standard does not mention any of these tools, yet each of them exists to read, write or test the elements it defines.1,2 This article looks at each kind of tool from the HTML point of view: what markup it expects, what markup it produces, and which HTML rules still apply.

Section 2 covers CSS frameworks, section 3 JavaScript frameworks, section 4 server-side template engines, section 5 server-side rendering, section 6 REST and GraphQL APIs and section 7 browser testing tools. Section 8 joins them in one request-to-test walk-through, and sections 9 to 13 hold exercises, trivia, a playground, a quick reference and the references. Version numbers are the latest releases in the npm registry on the date of writing.3

1Introduction

1.1 HTML as the integration layer

Each technology in this article sits on one side of the document. CSS frameworks are style sheets plus conventions for class names and data-* attributes. JavaScript frameworks build and update DOM trees. Template engines and server-side rendering produce HTML text on a server. APIs deliver the data that ends up inside elements. Testing tools drive a real browser and then query the DOM that results.1,2,4 None of them replaces HTML, so the semantics, accessibility rules and parsing behaviour covered earlier in this series apply to their output in full.

1.2 Where the HTML is produced

The most useful single question to ask about any of these tools is where and when the HTML is produced. Osmani and Miller's survey of rendering on the web names the main options. Static rendering happens at build time. Server-side rendering (SSR) means "rendering an app on the server to send HTML, rather than JavaScript, to the client". Client-side rendering (CSR) means "rendering an app in a browser, using JavaScript to modify the DOM". Hydration means running client-side scripts to add state and interactivity to HTML that the server rendered.4

Table 1. Where each technology produces or uses HTML
TechnologyRunsInputOutput
CSS frameworkBrowser (style engine)Your HTML with framework class namesComputed styles; some ship JavaScript for widgets5,6
JavaScript frameworkBrowser, and the server when using SSRComponents (JSX or templates) and stateDOM nodes; HTML strings on the server7–9
Template engineServer (or build step)Template file and a data modelAn HTML string sent in the HTTP response10–13
SSR / static generationServer or build step, then browserFramework componentsComplete HTML, then hydration in the browser4
REST / GraphQL APIServerHTTP requestUsually JSON, which a script or template turns into HTML14,15
Testing toolOutside or inside the browserA test scriptPass or fail, from queries against the DOM16–18

1.3 A short history

The tools arrived in roughly three waves. In the first, Selenium began in 2004 when Jason Huggins at ThoughtWorks wrote a "JavaScriptTestRunner" for an internal application.19 Roy Fielding's 2000 doctoral dissertation, which named and defined the REST architectural style, gave web APIs their vocabulary.20 The second wave, between 2010 and 2015, produced most of the frameworks in this article. The third wave, from 2018 onwards, standardised browser automation and brought utility-first CSS and server rendering into the mainstream.

1.4 About the demos

The demos run inside sandboxed iframe elements, as in the earlier articles, so nothing they do can affect this page.35 The libraries they use (Bootstrap 5.3.9, Tailwind CSS 4.3.5, Foundation 6.9.0, Vue 3.5.45 and React 19.3.1) are stored compressed inside this file and expanded when the page opens. The code samples still reference the official CDN URLs, so you can copy them into your own pages unchanged. Angular, the template engines, the servers and the testing tools cannot run in a browser tab without a build step or a server, so those demos are teaching models that reproduce the real tools' behaviour. Wherever a model is used, its output was checked against the real tool, and the section says so.3

Reading tip. If a framework demo stays blank, your browser may not support DecompressionStream, which every current engine has supported since 2023.36 The code beside each demo is still correct.

2HTML and CSS frameworks

A CSS framework is a style sheet written in advance, plus a set of naming conventions for the HTML that uses it. You connect it to a page with an ordinary link element, and it does nothing until your markup carries its class names.5,37 Some frameworks also ship JavaScript for interactive widgets, which finds its targets through data-* attributes, the attributes HTML reserves for private data that a page's own scripts can read.38,39

2.1 Component classes and utility classes

The three frameworks here take two different approaches. Bootstrap and Foundation are component frameworks: a class such as .btn or .callout names a whole component and switches on many declarations at once. In Bootstrap 5.3.9, the .btn rule sets 33 declarations, most of them CSS custom properties, and .btn-primary sets 14 more.40 Tailwind CSS is utility-first. Its documentation describes "combining many single-purpose presentational classes (utility classes) directly in your markup", so each class maps to roughly one declaration.6 Adam Wathan's 2017 essay argued that "separation of concerns" between HTML and CSS is less useful than it looks, since component class names tie the CSS to the markup's structure anyway.29

Both approaches leave the choice of elements to you, and that is where HTML knowledge matters. A framework can make a div look like a button, but only a button element is focusable, activates with the keyboard and is announced as a button by assistive technology without extra work.41,42

Don't

Looks like a button, is not oneHTML
<div class="btn btn-primary" onclick="save()">Save</div>

Not focusable, ignores Enter and Space, and has no button role.

Do

A real button with framework stylingHTML
<button type="button" class="btn btn-primary">Save</button>

The framework only styles it; the browser supplies the behaviour.41

2.2 Bootstrap

Bootstrap was created at Twitter in mid-2010 by Mark Otto and Jacob Thornton, was first called Twitter Blueprint, and was released on 19 August 2011.22 Version 5 "dropped jQuery for regular JavaScript".22 The current release is 5.3.9.31 The quick start adds one style sheet in the head and one script bundle, which includes Popper for positioning dropdowns, popovers and tooltips, before </body>.5

Bootstrap 5.3 from the jsDelivr CDNHTML
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>Bootstrap page</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap@5.3.9/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css"
        integrity="sha384-yEPZ7jP9S0QKiUQ0m3jjsO4ProIW7wvR9gXkI7JOGa2XVsw53Yke2bsdkBbjmmiX" crossorigin="anonymous">
</head>
<body>
  <!-- content -->
  <script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap@5.3.9/dist/js/bootstrap.bundle.min.js"
          integrity="sha384-WyOxWvTyr1QaMPfiPJSv76iReVthorl5uWlFtZPyK0IEB0hGzo9y5Bp9mYanr8Bu" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>
</body>
</html>

The integrity attribute holds a Subresource Integrity hash: the browser refuses to apply the file if its contents do not match, which protects you if the CDN is compromised. The hashes above were computed from the files in the published 5.3.9 package.31,43 The crossorigin="anonymous" attribute is needed because integrity checks on cross-origin files require a CORS request.43,44

Bootstrap's grid is "built with flexbox and is fully responsive", with 12 template columns per row.45 It has six default breakpoints: xs (below 576px, written without an infix), sm ≥576px, md ≥768px, lg ≥992px, xl ≥1200px and xxl ≥1400px.46 A class such as col-md-4 therefore means "one third of the row from 768px up, full width below". Interactive components are wired up declaratively: data-bs-toggle="collapse" and data-bs-target on a button tell the bundle which element to show and hide, and the component keeps aria-expanded in step with the state.38,39

Running in a sandboxed frame (scripts on)

On a desktop screen the frame is wider than 576px but narrower than 768px, so the navbar is expanded (navbar-expand-sm) while the cards still stack (col-md-4). On a phone the navbar collapses behind a toggler; click it to see the bundle change aria-expanded. Note that the markup is still semantic: a labelled nav, a main, article cards and real buttons. Bootstrap's h5 class lets a heading keep its correct level (h2) while looking smaller.40,47

2.3 Tailwind CSS

Tailwind CSS v4.0 was released on 22 January 2025 and is a ground-up rewrite. Configuration moved from a JavaScript file into CSS: a single @import "tailwindcss"; line replaces the old @tailwind directives, and design tokens are declared in an @theme block, which turns them into CSS custom properties such as --color-avocado-500.34 The release notes report full builds "up to 5x faster" and incremental builds "over 100x faster" than v3.34 The current release is 4.3.5.48

Tailwind normally runs as a build step that scans your HTML, JSX or template files for class names and writes a style sheet containing only the utilities you used.6,34 For prototypes it also offers a browser build, loaded with one script element, which watches the DOM and generates styles at run time; it is not intended for production.49 Variants are prefixes: hover:bg-sky-700 applies only on hover, and a breakpoint prefix such as md: applies from that width up. Tailwind is mobile-first: unprefixed utilities "take effect on all screen sizes". The default breakpoints are sm 40rem (640px), md 48rem (768px), lg 64rem (1024px), xl 80rem (1280px) and 2xl 96rem (1536px).6,50

Tailwind CSS: the same card with utilities (real Tailwind 4.3.5 browser build)HTML
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@tailwindcss/browser@4.3.5"></script>
<style type="text/tailwindcss">
  @theme { --color-brand: #2457a6; }
</style>
<main class="mx-auto max-w-xl p-4 font-sans">
  <h1 class="mb-3 text-2xl font-bold text-slate-800">Teashop</h1>
  <div class="grid gap-3 sm:grid-cols-2">
    <article class="rounded-xl border border-slate-200 p-4 shadow-sm">
      <h2 class="text-lg font-semibold">Blue mug</h2>

                     focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-brand">
        Add to basket</button>
    </article>
    <article class="rounded-xl border border-slate-200 p-4 opacity-75">
      <h2 class="text-lg font-semibold">Red teapot
        <span class="ml-1 rounded-full bg-red-100 px-2 text-sm text-red-700">Sold out</span></h2>
      <p class="mb-3 text-slate-600">Cast iron, 1 litre.</p>
      <button type="button" disabled class="rounded-lg bg-slate-300 px-4 py-2 text-slate-600 disabled:cursor-not-allowed">
        Add to basket</button>
    </article>
  </div>

</main>
Running in a sandboxed frame (scripts on)

The @theme block defines a brand colour, which immediately produces bg-brand and outline-brand utilities. Tab to the first button to see the focus-visible: outline; many utility-styled buttons in the wild forget it. The two columns appear when the frame is at least 640px wide, so on narrow screens the cards stack (sm:grid-cols-2).34,50

2.4 Foundation

Foundation was developed by the design agency ZURB, released in September 2011 and open-sourced under the MIT licence with version 2.0 in October 2011. It has been maintained by volunteers since 2019.23 Foundation for Sites 6 is the current line, at version 6.9.0.51 Its default layout system is the XY Grid, "a fully reworked new grid system in v6.4" built with flexbox; the number of columns is set by the $grid-columns Sass variable, which defaults to 12.52 The compiled style sheet defines breakpoints named small (0), medium (40em, 640px), large (64em, 1024px), xlarge (75em) and xxlarge (90em), and class names follow those names, as in medium-6.53 The installation guide loads foundation.min.css and foundation.min.js from jsDelivr. Its starter template loads jQuery first and calls $(document).foundation() to start the JavaScript plugins, and it asks for a no-js class on the html element.54

Foundation: XY Grid, callout and buttons (real Foundation 6.9.0 CSS)HTML

  <div class="grid-x grid-margin-x">

        <h2 class="h5">Blue mug</h2>

        <p>Cast iron, 1 litre.</p>

Rendered in a sandboxed frame

This demo uses only the style sheet: Foundation's JavaScript plugins depend on jQuery, which is not bundled here.54 Like Bootstrap, Foundation provides heading-size classes (h3, h5) so the visual size can differ from the element's level.53

2.5 Comparing the three

Table 3. Bootstrap, Tailwind CSS and Foundation compared
BootstrapTailwind CSSFoundation for Sites
ApproachComponents + utilitiesUtility-firstComponents + XY Grid
Latest version5.3.9314.3.5486.9.051
Grid12 columns, flexbox45CSS grid and flex utilities612 columns (configurable), flexbox52
Breakpoints576 / 768 / 992 / 1200 / 1400 px46640 / 768 / 1024 / 1280 / 1536 px50640 / 1024 / 1200 / 1440 px53
JavaScriptOwn bundle, no jQuery22None for styling; a build step generates the CSS34Plugins that use jQuery54
CustomisingSass variables, CSS custom properties40@theme in CSS34Sass settings52
HTML hooksClasses, data-bs-*39Classes only6Classes, data-* plugin attributes54
Which one? Pick Bootstrap or Foundation when you want ready-made, consistent components with little CSS of your own. Pick Tailwind when you write your own components, often in a JavaScript framework, and want the styles to sit next to the markup. With any of them, check the generated HTML for semantics: the frameworks style elements, they do not choose them for you.41,42

3HTML and JavaScript frameworks

The previous article on HTML APIs built interfaces by calling DOM methods one at a time: create an element, set its text, append it, remember to update it later. JavaScript frameworks replace those steps with a declarative description. You write what the HTML should look like for a given state, and the framework works out which DOM operations turn the current page into that HTML.7,55,56 The output is still ordinary DOM nodes, built from the same Document and Element interfaces that a hand-written script uses.2

3.1 Declarative rendering

All three examples below render the same product list: a checkbox filter, a list with a disabled button for sold-out items, and a basket count in a role="status" region. Comparing them shows how each framework expresses the same HTML.

3.2 React and JSX

React was created by Jordan Walke at Facebook, first used on the News Feed in 2011 and open-sourced at JSConf US in May 2013.24 The current version is 19.3.1.33 React components are JavaScript functions that return JSX, an HTML-like syntax extension. JSX is stricter than HTML: a component must return a single root (or a fragment, <>…</>), every tag must be closed, so <img> becomes <img />, and attributes use JavaScript names, such as className because class is a reserved word.58 htmlFor replaces for on label and output.59 createRoot() "lets you create a root to display React components inside a browser DOM node".7

ProductList.jsxJS
import { useState } from "react";
import { createRoot } from "react-dom/client";

const products = [
  { id: 1, name: "Blue mug", price: 8.5, inStock: true },
  { id: 2, name: "Red teapot", price: 24, inStock: false },
  { id: 3, name: "Green cup", price: 6, inStock: true },
];

function ProductList({ items }) {
  const [onlyInStock, setOnlyInStock] = useState(false);
  const [basket, setBasket] = useState(0);
  const shown = onlyInStock ? items.filter((p) => p.inStock) : items;
  return (
    <section aria-labelledby="h">
      <h2 id="h">Products</h2>
      <label htmlFor="stock">
        <input id="stock" type="checkbox" checked={onlyInStock}
               onChange={(e) => setOnlyInStock(e.target.checked)} /> In stock only
      </label>
      <ul>
        {shown.map((p) => (
          <li key={p.id} className={p.inStock ? "in" : "out"}>
            {p.name}: £{p.price.toFixed(2)}{" "}
            <button type="button" disabled={!p.inStock}
                    onClick={() => setBasket((n) => n + 1)}>Add</button>
          </li>
        ))}
      </ul>
      <p role="status">Basket: {basket} item{basket === 1 ? "" : "s"}</p>
    </section>
  );
}

createRoot(document.getElementById("root")).render(<ProductList items={products} />);

Browsers cannot parse JSX, so a build tool compiles it into function calls before it reaches the page. The frame below runs that compiled form. It was produced by the esbuild compiler from the file above, with the factory renamed to h and reformatted for reading, and it runs on the real React 19.3.1.33,58

React 19: the compiled component running (real React)HTML
<style>body{font:15px system-ui,sans-serif} li.out{color:#888} li{margin:4px 0}</style>
<div id="root"></div>
<!-- React 19 ships no UMD build, so react + react-dom are bundled for this article -->
<script src="react-19.3.1-bundle.js"></script>
<script>
  const h = React.createElement, { useState } = React;
  const products = [
    { id: 1, name: "Blue mug", price: 8.5, inStock: true },
    { id: 2, name: "Red teapot", price: 24, inStock: false },
    { id: 3, name: "Green cup", price: 6, inStock: true },
  ];
  function ProductList({ items }) {
    const [onlyInStock, setOnlyInStock] = useState(false);
    const [basket, setBasket] = useState(0);
    const shown = onlyInStock ? items.filter((p) => p.inStock) : items;
    return h("section", { "aria-labelledby": "h" },
      h("h2", { id: "h" }, "Products"),
      h("label", { htmlFor: "stock" },
        h("input", { id: "stock", type: "checkbox", checked: onlyInStock,
                     onChange: (e) => setOnlyInStock(e.target.checked) }), " In stock only"),
      h("ul", null, shown.map((p) =>
        h("li", { key: p.id, className: p.inStock ? "in" : "out" },
          p.name, ": £", p.price.toFixed(2), " ",
          h("button", { type: "button", disabled: !p.inStock,
                        onClick: () => setBasket((n) => n + 1) }, "Add")))),
      h("p", { role: "status" }, "Basket: ", basket, " item", basket === 1 ? "" : "s"));
  }
  ReactDOM.createRoot(document.getElementById("root")).render(h(ProductList, { items: products }));
</script>
Running in a sandboxed frame (scripts on)

Two HTML details matter here. First, key gives each list item a stable identity, so React can move, insert or delete the right li when the filter changes instead of rewriting every row.60 Second, React escapes every string it puts into the DOM. The only way to insert raw markup is the deliberately awkward dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: … }} prop, which the documentation says "should be used with extreme caution".59,61

3.3 Angular templates

Angular is "a web framework that empowers developers to build fast, reliable applications", maintained by a team at Google.56 It is the successor to AngularJS, which Miško Hevery created and Google first released in 2010; AngularJS long-term support ended on 31 December 2021.21 The current version is 22.2.6.28 Since version 22, Angular publishes a major release every 12 months (previously every six), and each major release is typically supported for 24 months.62

An Angular component is a TypeScript class with a @Component decorator that names its selector (the custom element name used in HTML), its template and optional styles. Components have been standalone by default since version 19.57 Templates are HTML extended with bindings: {{ }} for text, [property] for DOM properties, (event) for listeners and [(ngModel)] for two-way binding, a syntax the Angular community calls "banana-in-a-box".63,64 Since version 17, built-in control flow blocks replace the older structural directives: @if, @for with a track expression that uniquely identifies each item, and @switch.28,65

product-list.component.tsJS
import { Component, signal, computed } from "@angular/core";
import { CurrencyPipe } from "@angular/common";

@Component({
  selector: "app-products",
  imports: [CurrencyPipe],
  template: `
    <label><input type="checkbox" [checked]="onlyInStock()"
                  (change)="onlyInStock.set($any($event.target).checked)"> In stock only</label>
    <ul>
      @for (p of shown(); track p.id) {
        <li [class.out]="!p.inStock">{{ p.name }}: {{ p.price | currency:'GBP' }}
          <button type="button" [disabled]="!p.inStock" (click)="add()">Add</button></li>
      } @empty {
        <li>Nothing in stock.</li>
      }
    </ul>
    <p role="status">Basket: {{ basket() }}</p>`,
})
export class ProductList {
  items = [{ id: 1, name: "Blue mug", price: 8.5, inStock: true },
           { id: 2, name: "Red teapot", price: 24, inStock: false }];
  onlyInStock = signal(false);
  basket = signal(0);
  shown = computed(() => this.onlyInStock() ? this.items.filter(p => p.inStock) : this.items);
  add() { this.basket.update(n => n + 1); }
}

Angular normally compiles templates ahead of time with its CLI. The frame below runs the same component on the real Angular 22.2.6, using the just-in-time compiler that ships in @angular/compiler. Because a plain script cannot use TypeScript decorators, the decorator is applied as a function call, which is what TypeScript compiles a decorator to.28,57

Angular 22: the same component compiled in the browser (real Angular)HTML
<style>body{font:15px system-ui,sans-serif} li.out{color:#888} li{margin:4px 0}</style>
<app-products>Loading Angular…</app-products>
<!-- @angular/core, common, platform-browser and compiler, bundled for this article -->
<script src="angular-22.2.6-jit-bundle.js"></script>
<script>
  const { Component, signal, computed, CurrencyPipe, bootstrapApplication,
          provideZonelessChangeDetection, enableProdMode } = ngLite;
  enableProdMode();
  class ProductList {
    items = [{ id: 1, name: "Blue mug", price: 8.5, inStock: true },
             { id: 2, name: "Red teapot", price: 24, inStock: false }];
    onlyInStock = signal(false);
    basket = signal(0);
    shown = computed(() => this.onlyInStock() ? this.items.filter(p => p.inStock) : this.items);
    add() { this.basket.update(n => n + 1); }
  }
  Component({
    selector: "app-products",
    imports: [CurrencyPipe],
    template: `
      <label><input type="checkbox" [checked]="onlyInStock()"
                    (change)="onlyInStock.set($event.target.checked)"> In stock only</label>
      <ul>
        @for (p of shown(); track p.id) {
          <li [class.out]="!p.inStock">{{ p.name }}: {{ p.price | currency:'GBP' }}
            <button type="button" [disabled]="!p.inStock" (click)="add()">Add</button></li>
        } @empty { <li>Nothing in stock.</li> }
      </ul>
      <p role="status">Basket: {{ basket() }}</p>`,
  })(ProductList);
  bootstrapApplication(ProductList, { providers: [provideZonelessChangeDetection()] });
</script>
Running in a sandboxed frame (scripts on)

Look at the rendered DOM in your browser's developer tools and you will find empty comment nodes (<!---->) inside the ul. Angular uses comments as anchors that mark where a control-flow block's content starts and ends, and the root element gains an ng-version attribute.2,65 This is a reminder that framework output is real HTML with real nodes, including some you did not write.

3.4 Vue templates

Evan You created Vue in 2014 "as a personal side project".25 Vue calls itself "The Progressive Framework" because it can be adopted gradually, from "enhancing static HTML without a build step" to full single-page applications.55 The current version is 3.5.45; Vue 3.0.0 was published on 18 September 2020.66 Vue templates are valid HTML. Text uses "Mustache" syntax, {{ msg }}; v-bind:id binds an attribute and has the shorthand :id; and v-on:click listens for events, with the shorthand @click.67

Vue 3: an in-DOM template enhanced without a build step (real Vue 3.5.45)HTML
<style>body{font:15px system-ui,sans-serif} li.out{color:#888} li{margin:4px 0}</style>
<div id="app">
  <label><input type="checkbox" v-model="onlyInStock"> In stock only</label>
  <ul>
    <li v-for="p in shown" :key="p.id" :class="{ out: !p.inStock }">
      {{ p.name }}: £{{ p.price.toFixed(2) }}
      <button type="button" :disabled="!p.inStock" @click="basket++">Add</button>
    </li>
  </ul>
  <p role="status">Basket: {{ basket }}</p>
</div>
<script src="https://unpkg.com/vue@3.5.45/dist/vue.global.prod.js"></script>
<script>
  const { createApp, ref, computed } = Vue;
  createApp({
    setup() {
      const items = [{ id: 1, name: "Blue mug", price: 8.5, inStock: true },
                     { id: 2, name: "Red teapot", price: 24, inStock: false }];
      const onlyInStock = ref(false), basket = ref(0);
      const shown = computed(() => onlyInStock.value ? items.filter(p => p.inStock) : items);
      return { onlyInStock, basket, shown };
    },
  }).mount("#app");
</script>
Running in a sandboxed frame (scripts on)

Because this template lives inside the page, the browser's HTML parser reads it before Vue does. That has consequences the Vue guide lists as in-DOM template parsing caveats: HTML attribute names are case-insensitive, so camelCase props must be written in kebab-case; custom component tags need explicit closing tags; and elements such as ul, table and select only allow certain children, so a component inside a table must be written as <tr is="vue:my-row">.68,69 Single-file components (.vue files) avoid these caveats because a build tool compiles them. Vue also has an escape hatch for raw markup, v-html; the guide's advice is to use it "only on trusted content and never on user-provided content".67

3.5 The same HTML in three dialects

Table 4. How React, Angular and Vue write common HTML patterns
PatternReact (JSX)AngularVue
Text{name}{{ name }}{{ name }}
Attribute / propertydisabled={!ok}[disabled]="!ok":disabled="!ok"
ARIA or other attributearia-label={x}[attr.aria-label]="x":aria-label="x"
ClassclassName="a"[class.out]="!p.inStock":class="{ out: !p.inStock }"
LabelhtmlFor="id"for="id"for="id"
EventonClick={fn}(click)="fn()"@click="fn"
Condition{ok && <p/>}@if (ok) { … }v-if="ok"
Listitems.map(i => <li key={i.id}>)@for (i of items; track i.id)v-for="i in items" :key="i.id"
Two-way inputvalue + onChange[(ngModel)]="x"v-model="x"
Raw HTMLdangerouslySetInnerHTML[innerHTML] (sanitised)v-html

Sources: React JSX and common component reference; Angular binding, two-way binding and control flow guides; Vue template syntax guide.58,59,63–65,67 Angular sanitises values bound to innerHTML by removing unsafe markup.70

Frameworks do not fix markup. A component that renders <div onClick> is just as inaccessible as hand-written HTML, and a list rendered without ul and li loses its list semantics. Framework templates are HTML, and the rules from the semantic HTML article apply to them unchanged.41,42

4HTML and server-side templating

Long before component frameworks, servers produced HTML by filling gaps in a text file with data. A template engine takes a template and a data model and returns a string, which the server sends as the body of an HTTP response with a text/html content type.10,71 The browser cannot tell a template-generated page from a hand-written one; it parses whatever bytes arrive.69 Template engines remain the normal way to build pages in Java (Spring), Python (Flask, Django) and Node.js (Express) applications.72–74

4.1 How a template engine works

Escaping is the most important thing a template engine does. If a user's name is Ada <admin>, inserting it unescaped creates an element called admin; if it is <img src=x onerror=…>, it runs a script. This is cross-site scripting (XSS), and OWASP's main defence is output encoding appropriate to the context the value lands in.61 All four engines escape by default in HTML contexts, and all four have a separate syntax for raw output. The raw syntax should only ever receive markup your own code produced.10,12,75,76 HTML escaping is only correct for element content and quoted attribute values. A value placed inside a script element, a style element, an unquoted attribute or a URL needs a different encoding.61

Table 5. The four engines at a glance
ThymeleafJinja2EJSHandlebars
LanguageJavaPythonJavaScriptJavaScript (ports exist for other languages)
StyleAttributes on real HTML ("natural templates")Text with {{ }} and {% %} tagsText with embedded JavaScriptText with {{ }} tags and helpers
Escaped outputth:text, [[…]]{{ x }} (with autoescape on)<%= x %>{{x}}
Raw outputth:utext, [(…)]{{ x|safe }}<%- x %>{{{x}}}
Loopth:each="i : ${items}"{% for i in items %}<% items.forEach(…) %>{{#each items}}
Reuseth:fragment, th:insert, th:replace{% extends %}, {% block %}, {% include %}<%- include('file') %>Partials {{> name}}
Typical hostSpring BootFlaskExpressExpress, static site generators
Version checked3.1.63.1.67.0.2774.7.1078

Sources: Thymeleaf tutorial; Jinja template designer and API documentation; EJS README; Handlebars guide; Spring Boot, Flask and Express documentation.10–13,72–74,76,79 Thymeleaf and Jinja2 versions are those of the Maven Central and PyPI packages used to test this section.80,81

The four sections that follow use one example: a product page for the data below. Note the & in the title, the angle brackets in the user name, and the deliberately trusted HTML in promo. All four templates were run on the real engines (versions in Table 5), and all four produce the same HTML, apart from one extra span in the Thymeleaf version.

data.json: the model passed to every templateJSON
{
  "title": "Mugs & Teapots",
  "user": { "name": "Ada <admin>" },
  "items": [
    { "name": "Blue mug",   "price": 8.5, "inStock": true },
    { "name": "Red teapot", "price": 24,  "inStock": false }
  ],
  "promo": "<strong>Free delivery</strong> this week"
}

4.2 Thymeleaf

Thymeleaf describes itself as "a modern server-side Java template engine for both web and standalone environments".82 It was created, and is maintained, by the Galician software engineer Daniel Fernández.83 Its distinctive idea is the natural template: templates are HTML documents whose logic lives in th:* attributes, so the file "still looks and works like HTML" when opened directly in a browser or a design tool, with placeholder content standing in for the data.82 Out of the box it processes six template modes: HTML, XML, TEXT, JAVASCRIPT, CSS and RAW.10

products.html (Thymeleaf)HTML
<h1 th:text="${title}">Product list</h1>
<p>Hello, <span th:text="${user.name}">Customer</span>!</p>
<ul>
  <li th:each="item : ${items}" th:class="${item.inStock} ? 'in' : 'out'"
      th:inline="text">[[${item.name}]]: £[[${#numbers.formatDecimal(item.price, 1, 2)}]]<th:block th:unless="${item.inStock}"> (sold out)</th:block></li>
</ul>
<p th:utext="${promo}">Promotion</p>

Opened as a file, this shows "Product list", "Customer" and "Promotion". Processed, th:text replaces the element's content with the escaped value (this "is the default behaviour of the th:text attribute"), and th:utext, for "unescaped text", inserts it as markup.10 ${…} is a variable expression (OGNL in plain Thymeleaf, Spring EL inside Spring); *{…} selects properties of an object chosen with th:object; #{…} reads a message from a properties file for internationalisation; and @{…} builds a URL, as in th:href="@{/order/details(orderId=${o.id})}".10 th:block is an element that disappears from the output, which lets the template add logic without adding markup.10

ProductController.java (Spring Boot)Java
@Controller
class ProductController {
  @GetMapping("/products")
  String products(Model model) {
    model.addAttribute("title", "Mugs & Teapots");
    model.addAttribute("items", catalogue.findAll());
    return "products";          // renders src/main/resources/templates/products.html
  }
}

Spring Boot auto-configures Thymeleaf when the starter is on the class path and looks for templates in src/main/resources/templates.72 Shared layout is built from fragments: th:fragment="footer" names a piece of markup, th:insert="~{common :: footer}" places it inside the host element, and th:replace replaces the host element with it.10

4.3 Jinja2

Jinja, maintained by the Pallets project, uses three kinds of delimiters: {% … %} for statements, {{ … }} for expressions to print, and {# … #} for comments. Filters are applied with a pipe and can be chained, as in {{ name|striptags|title }}, and inside a loop a loop variable gives loop.index, loop.first and loop.last.11

products.html (Jinja2)Jinja
<h1>{{ title }}</h1>
<p>Hello, {{ user.name }}!</p>
<ul>
{% for item in items %}
  <li class="{{ 'in' if item.inStock else 'out' }}">{{ item.name }}: £{{ '%.2f'|format(item.price) }}{% if not item.inStock %} (sold out){% endif %}</li>
{% endfor %}
</ul>
<p>{{ promo|safe }}</p>

Two settings matter for HTML. First, autoescaping is off in a bare jinja2.Environment; the API documentation says "in future versions of Jinja we might enable autoescaping by default for security reasons" and recommends autoescape=select_autoescape(), which "enables autoescaping for HTML files".76 Flask turns it on for you: "autoescaping is enabled for all templates ending in .html, .htm, .xml, .xhtml, as well as .svg" when you use render_template().73 Second, block tags leave their own line breaks behind unless you set trim_blocks and lstrip_blocks, which the run that produced this section's output used.11

Jinja's strongest feature, in its own documentation's words, is template inheritance.11 A base template defines the document skeleton with named {% block %} regions, and child templates start with {% extends "base.html" %} and fill in only the blocks they change:

base.htmlJinja
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <title>{% block title %}Teashop{% endblock %}</title>
</head>
<body>
  <main>{% block content %}{% endblock %}</main>
</body>
</html>
products.html (child)Jinja
{% extends "base.html" %}
{% block title %}Products · {{ super() }}{% endblock %}
{% block content %}
  <h1>{{ title }}</h1>
  …
{% endblock %}
app.py (Flask)Python
from flask import Flask, render_template
app = Flask(__name__)

@app.get("/products")
def products():
    return render_template("products.html", **load_catalogue())   # autoescaped

4.4 EJS

EJS, "Embedded JavaScript templates", is "a simple templating language that lets you generate HTML markup with plain JavaScript".12,84 Its tags are few: <% for control flow with no output, <%= which "outputs the value into the template (escaped)", <%- which "outputs the unescaped value", <%# for comments, and <%_ / _%> and -%> for trimming whitespace.12 Because the code inside the tags is ordinary JavaScript, there is no template language to learn, but also nothing to stop business logic creeping into views.

products.ejsEJS
<h1><%= title %></h1>
<p>Hello, <%= user.name %>!</p>
<ul>
<%_ items.forEach(function (item) { _%>
  <li class="<%= item.inStock ? 'in' : 'out' %>"><%= item.name %>: £<%= item.price.toFixed(2) %><% if (!item.inStock) { %> (sold out)<% } %></li>
<%_ }) _%>
</ul>
<p><%- promo %></p>
server.js (Express)JS
import express from "express";
const app = express();
app.set("view engine", "ejs");                 // looks in ./views by default
app.get("/products", (req, res) => {
  res.render("products", loadCatalogue());     // views/products.ejs
});
app.listen(3000);

In Express, the view engine setting names the template engine to use, and res.render() renders a view with a data object and sends the result.74 Includes are written <%- include('user/show') %>, and their paths are resolved relative to the template that calls them. The include uses the unescaped tag because its output is already HTML.12

4.5 Handlebars

Handlebars, "minimal templating on steroids", is "largely compatible with Mustache templates", and its syntax "is a superset of Mustache templates".85 Values in {{expression}} "are HTML-escaped", while the triple-stash {{{expression}}} outputs them raw.75 Logic is limited on purpose. You cannot write arbitrary JavaScript in a template; instead you call helpers. The built-in helpers are #if, #unless, #each, #with, lookup and log, and anything else, such as formatting a price, is a helper you register in JavaScript.13,86

products.hbsHandlebars
<h1>{{title}}</h1>
<p>Hello, {{user.name}}!</p>
<ul>
{{#each items}}
  <li class="{{#if inStock}}in{{else}}out{{/if}}">{{name}}: £{{money price}}{{#unless inStock}} (sold out){{/unless}}</li>
{{/each}}
</ul>
<p>{{{promo}}}</p>
render.jsJS
import Handlebars from "handlebars";
Handlebars.registerHelper("money", (n) => n.toFixed(2));
Handlebars.registerPartial("footer", "<footer>© Teashop</footer>");   // used as {{> footer}}
const render = Handlebars.compile(source);    // compile once …
const html = render(data);                    // … render many times

Partials must be registered with Handlebars.registerPartial before use and are called with {{> name}}.79 In the test run, Handlebars dropped the lines that contain only a block tag, such as {{#each items}}, following the Mustache rule for "standalone" tags. EJS needed the <%_ _%> trimming tags to produce the same output.12,85,87

For the data above, their output matches what the real engines produced, character for character. The rendered pane is a sandboxed frame without scripts, so injected handlers cannot run.35,61

5HTML and server-side rendering


Section 3 rendered components in the browser, so the HTML sent by the server was little more than an empty <div id="root"> and a script. That is client-side rendering. Section 4 rendered pages on the server, but the result had no client-side behaviour. Server-side rendering with a JavaScript framework combines the two. The same components run on the server to produce complete HTML, and then run again in the browser to attach event handlers and state to that HTML, a step called hydration.4,88



5.1 Rendering strategies



Table 6. Where and when the HTML is produced

StrategyHTML producedFirst response containsTypical trade-off



Client-side rendering (CSR)In the browser, by JavaScriptAn empty shell and script tagsNothing useful appears until the JavaScript has downloaded and run4


Server-side rendering (SSR)On the server, per requestFull HTMLFast first paint, but rendering on the server "can increase your page's TTFB"4


Static rendering (SSG)At build timeFull HTML from a file or CDN"A consistently fast TTFB", but only for content known at build time4


Streaming SSROn the server, in chunksThe start of the HTML, then more as it is readySends "HTML in chunks that the browser can progressively render"4,8


SSR + hydrationServer, then browserFull HTML plus the framework codeHydration "can have a significant negative impact on TBT and INP, even if it improves FCP"4


Islands / partial hydrationServer; only some regions hydrateMostly static HTML with interactive islandsLess JavaScript; the page must be split into independent widgets89,90







5.2 Hydration, step by step


React's server API includes renderToString, the older non-streaming renderer, and the streaming renderers renderToPipeableStream (Node.js streams) and renderToReadableStream (Web Streams).8 On the client, hydrateRoot "lets you display React components inside a browser DOM node whose HTML content was previously generated by react-dom/server".88 Hydration does not rebuild the DOM. React walks the existing nodes, checks that they match what the components would render, and attaches event listeners. The documentation is blunt about mismatches: hydrateRoot() "expects the rendered content to be identical with the server-rendered content. You should treat mismatches as bugs and fix them."88


The frame below performs all three steps with the real React 19.3.1, using the browser build of renderToString to play the server. Click the counter after step 2: nothing happens, because the HTML has no listeners yet. After step 3 the same button works, and the DOM node is the same object as before. Tick "mismatch" to make the server and client render different text and see how React reports it.



SSR and hydration with real React 19.3.1HTML
<style>
  body { font: 14px system-ui, sans-serif; } button { font: inherit; }
  #root { border: 2px dashed #b4441f; padding: 8px 12px; margin: 8px 0; min-height: 40px; }
  pre { background: #f5f3ee; padding: 8px; white-space: pre-wrap; font-size: 12px; margin: 6px 0; }
</style>
<p><button id="s1">1. Render on "server"</button> <button id="s2" disabled>2. Send HTML</button>
   <button id="s3" disabled>3. Hydrate</button> <label><input type="checkbox" id="mm"> mismatch</label></p>
<div id="root"></div>
<pre id="log">Server output will appear here.</pre>
<script src="react-19.3.1-bundle.js"></script>
<script>
  const h = React.createElement, log = (m) => (document.getElementById("log").textContent += "\n" + m);
  let isServer = true, html = "", firstButton;
  function Counter({ start }) {
    const [n, setN] = React.useState(start);
    const where = document.getElementById("mm").checked ? (isServer ? "server" : "client") : "both";
    return h("p", null, "Rendered on: ", where, " ",
      h("button", { type: "button", onClick: () => setN(n + 1) }, "Clicked ", n, " times"));
  }
  s1.onclick = () => {
    isServer = true;
    html = ReactDOMServer.renderToString(h(Counter, { start: 0 }));
    document.getElementById("log").textContent = "renderToString() returned:\n" + html;
    s2.disabled = false;
  };
  s2.onclick = () => {
    root.innerHTML = html;                       // what the browser parses from the response
    firstButton = root.querySelector("button");
    log("HTML inserted. Try the button: no listeners yet.");
    s3.disabled = false;
  };
  s3.onclick = () => {
    isServer = false;
    ReactDOM.hydrateRoot(root, h(Counter, { start: 0 }), {
      onRecoverableError: (err) => log("Recoverable error: " + String(err.message).split("\n")[0]),
    });
    setTimeout(() => log("Hydrated. Same <button> node as before? " +
      (root.querySelector("button") === firstButton)), 50);
    s3.disabled = true;
  };
</script>
Running in a sandboxed frame (scripts on)


With "mismatch" ticked, React reports a recoverable hydration error and re-renders the root on the client, so the button is no longer the node the server sent. In a real application that means wasted work and a visible flash. Common causes are values that differ between server and client, such as dates, random IDs, window checks and locale-dependent formatting, and invalid HTML nesting that the browser's parser repairs differently from the framework's expectations, such as a div inside a p.69,88



5.3 Rendering timeline simulator


This model estimates when content becomes visible and when it becomes interactive under each strategy. It uses a simple formula: round trips cost the chosen latency, downloads cost size divided by bandwidth, and JavaScript costs size multiplied by a CPU factor. The numbers are illustrative, not measurements, but the model reproduces the qualitative trade-offs described in Rendering on the Web.4




  

    
    
    
    
    
  

  

  





5.4 SSR in the frameworks


Few teams wire up renderToString and hydrateRoot by hand. Each framework has a server-rendering setup, often provided by a "meta-framework" built on top of it.


    

  • React and Next.js. In the Next.js App Router, "by default, layouts and pages are Server Components": they render only on the server and send no component code to the browser. A file opts in to client-side interactivity with the "use client" directive at the top, above its imports.91 The current Next.js release is 16.4.6.92
    • 

  • Vue and Nuxt. Vue's server renderer is exposed under vue/server-renderer; renderToString() "takes a Vue app instance and returns a Promise that resolves to the rendered HTML". The client creates the app with createSSRApp, and mount() then hydrates instead of re-rendering. The Vue guide recommends using a framework with built-in SSR support, such as Nuxt (currently 4.6.4), rather than building it yourself.9,93
    • 

  • Angular. ng new --ssr creates a server-rendered project and ng add @angular/ssr converts an existing one. By default Angular prerenders the whole application, and each route can choose RenderMode.Server, RenderMode.Client or RenderMode.Prerender.94 Hydration "restores the server-side rendered application on the client" and is enabled with provideClientHydration().95 Incremental hydration can leave parts of the page dehydrated until a trigger fires, written as @defer (hydrate on viewport) { … }, with triggers such as idle, viewport, interaction, hover and timer.90
    • 




Vue SSR in a few lines (server and client)JS
// app.js: shared by server and client
import { createSSRApp } from "vue";
export const createApp = () => createSSRApp({
  data: () => ({ count: 1 }),
  template: `<button @click="count++">{{ count }}</button>`,
});

// server.js
import { renderToString } from "vue/server-renderer";
const html = await renderToString(createApp());
res.send(`<!doctype html><div id="app">${html}</div><script type="module" src="/client.js"></script>`);

// client.js: mount() on SSR markup hydrates it
createApp().mount("#app");



5.5 What SSR means for your HTML


    

  • The HTML must work on its own. Between first paint and hydration, or for ever if the script fails to load, only HTML behaviour exists. Links navigate, and forms submit with a real action and method. Designing for that first is called progressive enhancement, and it makes the hydration gap harmless.4,96
    • 

  • Data is sent twice. The server puts the data into the HTML and must also give it to the client so hydration renders the same output. It is usually serialised into a <script type="application/json"> element, which the HTML Standard allows as a data block that the browser does not execute. Any </script sequence inside the JSON must be escaped, or it ends the element early.61,97
    • 

  • Valid nesting matters more. The server writes text, and the browser's parser silently repairs invalid nesting, such as a p inside a p, so the DOM no longer matches what the framework expects to hydrate.69,88
    • 

  • Streaming works because HTML parses incrementally. The browser renders the parts of the document it has already received, so a server can flush the head and page shell before slow data is ready.8,69
    • 





6HTML and APIs


6.1 From forms to fetch()


HTML has been an API client from the start. A link makes a GET request and a form makes a GET or POST request with its fields encoded in the URL or the body, and the response replaces the page.71,96 Modern pages more often request data from a script and insert it into the existing document. The Fetch Standard, which "defines requests, responses, and the process that binds them: fetching", specifies the fetch() function they use and the CORS rules that decide when a page may read a response from another origin.44



Fetching JSON and rendering it into HTML safelyJS
const list = document.querySelector("#books");
const row = document.querySelector("#book-row");      // <template> with an <li>
list.setAttribute("aria-busy", "true");
try {
  const res = await fetch("/api/authors/1/books", { headers: { Accept: "application/json" } });
  if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);  // fetch does not reject on 404 or 500
  const books = await res.json();
  list.replaceChildren(...books.map((b) => {
    const li = row.content.firstElementChild.cloneNode(true);
    li.querySelector(".title").textContent = b.title;  // text, never innerHTML
    li.querySelector("time").textContent = b.year;
    li.querySelector("time").dateTime = String(b.year);
    return li;
  }));
} catch (err) {
  list.replaceChildren(Object.assign(document.createElement("li"), { textContent: "Could not load books." }));
} finally {
  list.removeAttribute("aria-busy");
}


Three details in this snippet recur in every API integration. First, fetch() "will reject the promise on some errors, but not if the server responds with an error status like 404", so the code must check response.ok, which is true only for statuses in the 200 range.98 Second, the data goes into the page with textContent and a cloned template, never by concatenating strings into innerHTML.61,99 Third, aria-busy tells assistive technology that the region is being updated.42



6.2 REST


Roy Fielding defined Representational State Transfer in his 2000 dissertation, Architectural Styles and the Design of Network-based Software Architectures.20 REST is a set of constraints, not a protocol: client–server, stateless, cache, uniform interface, layered system and, as "only an optional constraint", code-on-demand. The uniform interface is itself defined by four constraints: identification of resources, manipulation of resources through representations, self-descriptive messages, and "hypermedia as the engine of application state".14 MDN summarises REST as a group of "software architecture design constraints" that make distributed systems efficient, reliable and scalable.100


HTML is itself the original hypermedia format. An HTML page that a browser displays satisfies the last constraint directly: the representation carries its own links and forms, and the user moves the application forward by following them, without knowing any URLs in advance.14,96 Most JSON "REST APIs" keep the resource URLs and HTTP methods but leave out the hypermedia, so the client must know the URL scheme beforehand.




Table 7. HTTP methods in a typical REST API (semantics from RFC 9110)

MethodExampleMeaningSafeIdempotentFrom an HTML form?



GETGET /api/books/7Retrieve a representationYesYesYes


POSTPOST /api/booksProcess the enclosed data, e.g. createNoNoYes


PUTPUT /api/books/7Replace the resource's stateNoYesNo (script only)


PATCHPATCH /api/books/7Apply a partial modificationNoNoNo (script only)


DELETEDELETE /api/books/7Remove the resourceNoYesNo (script only)




Sources: RFC 9110 §9 (methods, safe and idempotent properties) and RFC 5789 (PATCH); HTML form method keywords are get, post and dialog.71,101,102



6.3 GraphQL


GraphQL "was created in 2012 and open sourced by Facebook in 2015", and since 2019 it has been governed by the GraphQL Foundation, hosted by the Linux Foundation.27 The specification has been published in editions since July 2015, and the latest release is the September 2026 edition.15 The reference implementation, graphql-js, is at version 17.1.0.103 A GraphQL server exposes a typed schema at a single endpoint, and the client sends a query that names exactly the fields it wants. The response has the same shape as the query. Operations are queries (reads), mutations (writes) and subscriptions (streams of events).15


The GraphQL over HTTP specification, still a working draft, says a server "MUST support GraphQL-over-HTTP request via POST" and may also support GET, but "GET requests MUST NOT be used for executing mutation operations". It registers application/graphql-response+json as the media type for responses.104 Errors usually come back in an errors array next to any data that could still be resolved, so, as with fetch() and a 404, a client must inspect the body rather than rely on the HTTP status alone.15,104



One GraphQL request for an author cardJS
const query = `query AuthorCard($id: ID!) {
  author(id: $id) { name books { title year rating } }
}`;
const res = await fetch("/graphql", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json", Accept: "application/graphql-response+json" },
  body: JSON.stringify({ query, variables: { id: "1" } }),
});
const { data, errors } = await res.json();
if (errors) console.warn(errors.map((e) => e.message));





6.4 REST and GraphQL explorer


Both APIs below run in this page against the same small in-memory data set; nothing leaves your browser. Load the author card each way and compare the number of requests and bytes. The GraphQL side runs a small executor written for this article. It supports field selection, nested objects and arguments, and reports unknown fields in an errors array as the specification describes.15 Try adding a field that does not exist.

7HTML and browser testing


Unit tests can check the functions that produce HTML, but only a browser can show whether the HTML works: whether the button is really a button, the label is really attached, and the page responds after hydration. Browser automation tools start a real browser, load the page, act like a user and then query the DOM.16–18 Each of them finds elements through selectors, roles, labels or text, so well-structured HTML makes tests both easier to write and more meaningful.105



7.1 Three architectures




7.2 Selenium and WebDriver


Selenium began in 2004, when Jason Huggins at ThoughtWorks built a "JavaScriptTestRunner" for an internal application. A standalone server version became "Selenium Remote Control", and Simon Stewart, also at ThoughtWorks, separately developed a tool called WebDriver; the two projects later merged.19 Selenium describes itself as "an umbrella project for a range of tools and libraries that enable and support the automation of web browsers", and its WebDriver API "drives a browser natively, as a user would, either locally or on a remote machine".107,109 Selenium 4.0.0 was released on 13 October 2021, and the JavaScript binding is now at 4.52.0.32,110


Selenium's lasting contribution is a standard. WebDriver became a W3C Recommendation on 5 June 2018, edited by Simon Stewart and David Burns, and the specification acknowledges that it "is derived from the popular Selenium WebDriver" framework.16,111 Every major browser now ships a driver that implements it, so a test written against WebDriver runs against any of them. WebDriver Level 2 is a W3C Working Draft. WebDriver BiDi, the "BiDirectional WebDriver Protocol", extends it with a WebSocket connection so the browser can push events such as console messages and network activity to the test.106,111 Since version 4.6, Selenium Manager, "a command-line tool implemented in Rust", downloads and caches the right driver automatically.112



products.test.js (selenium-webdriver)JS
import { Builder, By, until } from "selenium-webdriver";

const driver = await new Builder().forBrowser("chrome").build();   // Selenium Manager finds the driver
try {
  await driver.get("http://localhost:8123/products.html");
  const add = await driver.wait(until.elementLocated(By.css("li.in button")), 5000);
  await add.click();
  const status = await driver.findElement(By.css('[role="status"]'));
  await driver.wait(until.elementTextIs(status, "Basket: 1 item"), 5000);
} finally {
  await driver.quit();
}


Note the explicit waits. A WebDriver command acts immediately, so a test against a page that renders with JavaScript must wait for the element it needs, or it fails at random. This "flakiness" is the main problem the newer tools set out to solve.107,113



7.3 Playwright


Microsoft published Playwright 1.0.0 in May 2020, and it is now at 1.65.1.30 It "supports Chromium, WebKit and Firefox on Windows, Linux and macOS".17 Before each action, Playwright "auto-waits for all the relevant checks to pass and only then performs the requested action": the element must be attached, visible, stable, enabled and able to receive events. Its assertions retry automatically until they pass or time out.113 Its documentation recommends "prioritizing role locators", page.getByRole(), which find elements the way assistive technology does: by ARIA role and accessible name.105 npx playwright codegen records a test while you click through a site.114



tests/products.spec.js (@playwright/test)JS
const { test, expect } = require("@playwright/test");

test.beforeEach(async ({ page }) => {
  await page.goto("/products.html");
});

test("adds an in-stock product to the basket", async ({ page }) => {
  await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Add" }).first().click();
  await expect(page.getByRole("status")).toHaveText("Basket: 1 item");
});

test("sold-out products cannot be added", async ({ page }) => {
  const teapot = page.getByRole("listitem").filter({ hasText: "Red teapot" });
  await expect(teapot.getByRole("button", { name: "Add" })).toBeDisabled();
});

test("the filter hides sold-out products", async ({ page }) => {
  await page.getByLabel("In stock only").check();
  await expect(page.getByRole("listitem")).toHaveCount(2);
  await expect(page.getByText("Red teapot")).toBeHidden();
});


This suite was run with Playwright 1.63 against the React product list from section 3.2, served from a local web server. All three tests passed. A fourth test, with a deliberately wrong expectation ("Basket: 1 items"), produced the failure report below. The assertion retried for its five-second timeout, and the call log shows what the locator found each time.113,115



Output of npx playwright test (failing test, abridged)Text
  ✘  1 tests/fail.spec.js:7:1 › adds an in-stock product to the basket (5.2s)

    Error: expect(locator).toHaveText(expected) failed

    Locator:  getByRole('status')
    Expected: "Basket: 1 items"
    Received: "Basket: 1 item"
    Timeout:  5000ms

    Call log:
      - Expect "toHaveText" getByRole('status') with timeout 5000ms
      - waiting for getByRole('status')
        14 × locator resolved to <p role="status">Basket: 1 item</p>
           - unexpected value "Basket: 1 item"





7.4 Cypress


Cypress takes the opposite approach to Selenium. Its tests are "executed in the same run loop as your application", inside the browser, while Selenium-style tools operate "by running outside of the browser". It supports "Firefox and Chrome-family browsers (including Edge)".18 Every query, such as cy.get or cy.contains, and every assertion retries, by default "for up to 4 seconds", the defaultCommandTimeout setting.116 The in-browser design has documented trade-offs: "Cypress controls one browser at a time", new tabs are handled through a plugin, and "each test is bound to a single superdomain", with cy.origin() needed to visit another one.117 Cypress also mounts individual components for testing, with official libraries for React, Angular, Vue and Svelte.118 The current version is 16.3.0.119



cypress/e2e/products.cy.jsJS
describe("products", () => {
  beforeEach(() => cy.visit("/products.html"));

  it("adds an in-stock product to the basket", () => {
    cy.contains("li", "Blue mug").find("button").click();
    cy.get('[role="status"]').should("have.text", "Basket: 1 item");
  });

  it("the filter hides sold-out products", () => {
    cy.contains("label", "In stock only").click();
    cy.get("li").should("have.length", 2);
  });
});

RunsOutside the browser, via the W3C WebDriver protocol16,107Outside the browser, connected to each engine108Inside the browser, with a Node process18


BrowsersAny with a WebDriver driver107Chromium, Firefox, WebKit17Chrome family, Firefox18


LanguagesJava, Python, C#, Ruby, JavaScript…109JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, Java, .NET17JavaScript/TypeScript18


WaitingExplicit waitsAuto-wait + retrying assertions113Retry-ability, 4 s default116


Tabs and originsMultiple windowsMultiple pages and contextsOne tab; cy.origin() for other sites117


Component testsNoYes, mount fixture120Yes: React, Angular, Vue, Svelte118

7.5 Writing testable HTML


The locator you can use depends on the HTML you wrote. Playwright's list of built-in locators starts with role, label, placeholder, text, alt text and title, and ends with getByTestId(), which matches a data-testid attribute by default.105 The first group only works if the markup is semantic: getByRole("button", { name: "Add" }) finds a button, but not a div styled to look like one. A test that uses role locators therefore also checks part of the page's accessibility.42,105



Table 9. Locator strategies, from most to least user-facing

StrategyExampleNeeds in the HTMLBreaks when



Role + namegetByRole("button", { name: "Add" })Correct element or ARIA role; an accessible nameThe user-visible behaviour changes


LabelgetByLabel("Email")label associated with the controlThe label text changes


Textcy.contains("Blue mug")Visible textThe wording changes


Test IDgetByTestId("basket")data-testid="basket"Only if someone removes the attribute


CSS / XPathBy.css("li.in button")Specific classes and structureStyling or layout is refactored




Based on Playwright's locator guide and the Cypress and Selenium examples above.105,107,116 Framework class names make poor locators: col-md-4 or bg-blue-600 describe appearance, and change whenever the design does.6,45

Like Playwright, its locators find elements by role and accessible name, and it waits up to five seconds for elements and assertions.105,113 Use the switches to make the app load slowly (the test still passes, because it waits) or to replace the real button with a styled div (the role locator now fails, as it should).

8Putting it together


A realistic page uses most of these technologies at once. Follow one request for the product page through a typical stack, and notice that HTML is the only format every step shares.


    

  1. Request. The browser sends GET /products. The HTTP semantics are those of RFC 9110.71
    2. 

  2. Data. The server loads the catalogue, either from its own database or from a REST or GraphQL API.14,15
    3. 

  3. Server rendering. A template engine (section 4) or a framework's server renderer (section 5) turns the data into HTML. Every value is escaped, and the page includes the framework's style sheet, such as Bootstrap's with an integrity hash.43,61
    4. 

  4. First paint. The browser parses the HTML as it streams in and paints the page. Links and forms already work.4,69
    5. 

  5. Hydration. The framework's script attaches listeners to the existing DOM, reading the same data from a JSON data block so its output matches.88,97
    6. 

  6. Updates. Later interactions call fetch(), check response.ok and patch the DOM.98
    7. 

  7. Tests. In CI, Playwright, Cypress or Selenium loads the page in real browsers and checks it through roles and labels, so the semantics are tested along with the behaviour.16,18,105
    8. 




views/products.ejs: server-rendered page that a client component hydratesEJS
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>Products · Teashop</title>
  <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap@5.3.9/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css"
        integrity="sha384-yEPZ7jP9S0QKiUQ0m3jjsO4ProIW7wvR9gXkI7JOGa2XVsw53Yke2bsdkBbjmmiX" crossorigin="anonymous">
</head>
<body>
  <main class="container" id="root"><%- appHtml %></main>   <%# already escaped by the renderer %>
  <script type="application/json" id="initial-data"><%- json %></script>
  <script type="module" src="/client.js"></script>
</body>
</html>


The json value must be produced by a serialiser that escapes < (for example as \u003c), because a product named </script><script>… would otherwise close the data block and inject a script. This is the one place in the template where neither HTML escaping nor raw output is correct on its own.61,97




9Exercises


Try each exercise before opening its solution. The playground has the real frameworks loaded, and the template lab and API explorer can check your answers to exercises 3 and 6.





Exercise 1: Fix the framework markup


This Bootstrap snippet looks right but has three accessibility problems. Find and fix them.


Exercise 1HTML
<div class="card">
  <div class="card-body">
    <div class="h5">Blue mug</div>
    <img src="mug.jpg" class="img-fluid">
    <div class="btn btn-primary" onclick="add(1)">Add</div>
  </div>
</div>


Show solution


Solution 1HTML
<article class="card">
  <div class="card-body">
    <h2 class="h5">Blue mug</h2>
    <img src="mug.jpg" class="img-fluid" alt="Blue stoneware mug">
    <button type="button" class="btn btn-primary" onclick="add(1)">Add</button>
  </div>
</article>


(1) The title is a div, so it is not a heading; use the right level and keep the look with the h5 class. (2) The image has no alt. (3) The "button" is a div: not focusable and not announced as a button. Using article for a self-contained card is a further improvement.40,41,47









Exercise 2: Breakpoints


An element has class="col-12 col-md-6 col-xl-4" in Bootstrap. How wide is it in a 700px, 1000px and 1300px viewport? What would the closest Tailwind classes be?


Show solution


700px: full width (below md, 768px). 1000px: half (≥768, below xl, 1200px). 1300px: a third. In Tailwind, on a grid parent: col-span-12 md:col-span-6 xl:col-span-4 inside grid grid-cols-12. Tailwind's xl starts at 1280px, not 1200px, so a 1250px viewport would differ.45,46,50









Exercise 3: Escape or not?


For each engine, write the tag that outputs comment.body (user input) and the tag that outputs renderedMarkdown (HTML your server produced with a sanitiser).


Show solution




EngineUser input (escaped)Trusted HTML (raw)



Thymeleafth:text="${comment.body}"th:utext="${renderedMarkdown}"


Jinja2{{ comment.body }} (autoescape on){{ renderedMarkdown|safe }}


EJS<%= comment.body %><%- renderedMarkdown %>


Handlebars{{comment.body}}{{{renderedMarkdown}}}




In Jinja2 the escaped form is only safe if autoescaping is enabled, as Flask does for .html templates.10,12,73,75,76









Exercise 4: Translate the template


Rewrite this Vue template in React JSX and as an Angular template.


Exercise 4 (Vue)HTML
<ul>
  <li v-for="t in todos" :key="t.id" :class="{ done: t.done }">
    <label><input type="checkbox" v-model="t.done"> {{ t.title }}</label>
  </li>
</ul>
<p v-if="!todos.length">Nothing to do.</p>


Show solution


ReactJS
<>
  <ul>
    {todos.map((t) => (
      <li key={t.id} className={t.done ? "done" : undefined}>
        <label><input type="checkbox" checked={t.done} onChange={() => toggle(t.id)} /> {t.title}</label>
      </li>
    ))}
  </ul>
  {todos.length === 0 && <p>Nothing to do.</p>}
</>


AngularHTML
<ul>
  @for (t of todos(); track t.id) {
    <li [class.done]="t.done">
      <label><input type="checkbox" [checked]="t.done" (change)="toggle(t.id)"> {{ t.title }}</label>
    </li>
  }
</ul>
@if (!todos().length) { <p>Nothing to do.</p> }


React has no two-way binding, so the checkbox needs a controlled checked value and an onChange handler; the fragment <> gives the single root JSX requires.58,65,67









Exercise 5: Diagnose the hydration error


A Next.js page renders <p>Generated at {new Date().toLocaleTimeString()}</p> and another component renders <p><div>Note</div></p>. Both cause hydration warnings. Why?


Show solution


The time differs between the server render and the client render, so the text does not match; render it only on the client (after mount) or pass the server's value down as data. The second is invalid HTML: a div start tag implicitly closes an open p, so the browser's DOM is <p></p><div>Note</div><p></p>, which is not what React expects to find.69,88









Exercise 6: REST or GraphQL request count


A dashboard shows 10 authors, each with their 3 latest books and each book's average rating. With the REST API in section 6.4, how many requests are needed, and how many can run in parallel? How many with GraphQL?


Show solution


REST: 1 (list authors) + 10 (books per author) + 30 (reviews per book) = 41 requests in three dependent waves: the 10 book requests can run in parallel once the author list arrives, then the 30 review requests. GraphQL: 1 request, with the joining done on the server. A REST API could add an endpoint or an ?include= parameter to reduce this, at the cost of a less uniform interface.14,15









Exercise 7: Make it testable


This search form cannot be targeted with getByLabel or getByRole("button", { name: "Search" }). Fix the HTML, then write the Playwright test that types "mug" and checks that a role="status" region says "3 results".


Exercise 7HTML
<input type="text" placeholder="Search…" id="q">
<span class="icon-search" onclick="search()"></span>
<div class="results-count"></div>


Show solution


Solution 7 (HTML)HTML
<form role="search" action="/search">
  <label for="q">Search products</label>
  <input type="search" id="q" name="q">
  <button>Search</button>
</form>
<p role="status" class="results-count"></p>


Solution 7 (test)JS
await page.getByLabel("Search products").fill("mug");
await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Search" }).click();
await expect(page.getByRole("status")).toHaveText("3 results");


A real label, a real button inside a form, and a status region make the form usable by keyboard and screen reader users, and also give the test stable, user-facing locators. With JavaScript turned off, the form still submits to /search.41,42,105









Exercise 8: Choose a rendering strategy


Pick a strategy for (a) a documentation site updated weekly, (b) a product page with live stock levels, (c) a drawing application behind a login. Use the simulator to compare.


Show solution


(a) Static rendering: the content is known at build time, and CDN delivery gives a consistently fast TTFB. (b) SSR, possibly streamed, with the stock level as a small hydrated island or fetched after load, so the indexable HTML is complete. (c) Client-side rendering: there is no content to show before the application loads, it is not indexed by search engines, and interactivity matters more than first paint.4,89

Escape by default
Every engine and framework escapes text. Treat each raw-output feature (th:utext, |safe, <%-, {{{ }}}, v-html, dangerouslySetInnerHTML) as a security review item.61

  
Semantics survive frameworks
Frameworks style and generate elements; they do not choose them. Use button, label, headings and lists, then test with role locators.41,105

  
Pin and verify CDN files
Use exact versions with integrity and crossorigin, or self-host the files.5,43

  
Make the first HTML useful
Server-rendered links and forms should work before hydration; that is the cheapest performance and resilience win.4,96
